children: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (NASDAQ:VRTX) is navigating a packed regulatory and commercial calendar—povetacicept hits an FDA PDUFA on Nov. 30 with two‑year kidney follow‑up, pivotal pove/inaxaplin readouts and AMPLIFY Phase IIb data due this fall, a Crinetics buy expands endocrine assets, and JOURNAVX/ALYFTREK rollouts accelerate.
: VRTX faces an FDA PDUFA date on Nov. 30 for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy; drug targets APRIL and BAFF and has a monthly autoinjector formulation.
: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) faces near-term milestones: pivotal readouts for its pove and inaxaplin programs, scheduled data releases that mark key timeline-based clinical development events.

: Vertex (VRTX) will acquire Crinetics to expand its rare endocrine pipeline. Key programs cited: PALSONIFY for acromegaly and atumelnant for CAH and Cushing’s — potential multi‑billion-dollar assets.
: Vertex will collect two‑year kidney‑function follow‑up data for povetacicept, extending the timeline to align with global regulatory expectations outside the U.S.
: Vertex (VRTX) will report AMPLIFY Phase IIb AMKD top-line results this fall. Study includes type 2 diabetes cohort and modest-proteinuria group targeting a 20–30% proteinuria reduction signal.

: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) partners with Lindsey Vonn to promote JOURNAVX (suzetrigine), FDA‑approved Jan 30, 2025 for adult acute pain; JOURNAVX has >1 million U.S. prescriptions since approval.
: Vertex (VRTX) plans ALYFTREK rollout: shift patients from TRIKAFTA, expand to younger pediatric groups, and pursue reimbursement in emerging markets including Brazil and Turkey.
